sys_script_client.description: Polymorphic discriminator hygiene for x_casemgmt_case_party (verifier finding I2). On every change of party_type the script clears the reference column the new discriminator makes inapplicable - organization when party_type becomes Person, person when it becomes Organization - so the hidden field left behind by ../ui_policy/x_casemgmt_case_party_conditional_fields.xml cannot post a stale sys_id. Without it the classic form submits the hidden, non-disabled input verbatim (measured: party_type=Person with both the new person and the old organization on the wire), ../business_rules/x_casemgmt_validate_case_party_integrity.xml correctly refuses with "Organization must be empty when Party Type is Person." plus Invalid insert, and the user cannot clear the blocking value because the field is not on their screen - a dead end on any INSERT and on any UPDATE whose discriminator round-trips back to the stored value, since the rule normalises only a genuine update-conversion. A sys_ui_policy_action cannot do this: its `cleared` flag is one-way with no reverse, it would force one policy to act on the other's field and reinstate the contention the one-field-per-policy design removes, it would fire on load and so mutate stored data on a mere open, and a policy cannot see newValue/isLoading to restrict itself to an actual change. Clears the value and the reference display text together, never touches the applicable field, and returns having changed nothing on isLoading, on an empty party_type and on any discriminator value it does not recognise. The server-side rule remains the enforcing authority for every non-form write path. Per AAP Sections 0.4.3, 0.5.7 and 0.7.2.
sys_script_client.name: x_casemgmt_case_party_clear_opposite_ref
